title: The conductor ideal of normalization commutes with smooth pullback
statement:
Let $S$ be a reduced scheme of finite type over $\mathbf Q$ [def-pc-reduced-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $
u:S^
u	o S$ be its componentwise normalization [def-weil-pbc-reduced-normalization]. The map $
u$ is finite, the map $\mathcal O_S	o
u_*\mathcal O_{S^
u}$ is injective, and its cokernel $C_S$ is a coherent $\mathcal O_S$-module. Define $D_S=\operatorname{Ann}_{\mathcal O_S}(C_S)$, where a local section $a$ belongs to the annihilator if multiplication by $a$ on every local section of $C_S$ is zero. Then $D_S$ is a coherent ideal, and $V(D_S)$ is precisely the set of points whose local ring is not an integrally closed domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. This zero set is nowhere dense; $D_S=\mathcal O_S$ if and only if $S$ is normal. For every quasi-compact smooth $h:T	o S$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], $D_T=D_S\mathcal O_T$ as ideals in $\mathcal O_T$. This equality is compatible with identities and composition.

proof.text: Finite normalization and the dense normal open follow from reduced_algebraic_normalization_field_change over ULift Q. Local finite type over that field makes S locally Noetherian. Surjectivity implies dominance; reducedness of S makes the normalization schematically dominant, so every map on sections is injective. Coherence of the unit on S and on its finite normalization, finite pushforward coherence, and closure under cokernels give coherence of C_S.

source.place: Tags 035S and 0H7D; coherence of finite pushforward and cokernels.

proof.text: The scheme-theoretic-support ideal for the coherent C_S has affine ideals Ann(C_S(U)). Since ofIdeals recovers an existing compatible ideal family, it equals conductorIdeal S. Every ideal sheaf on a locally Noetherian scheme is coherent: its module is the kernel of the structure map to the pushforward of the structure sheaf of its closed subscheme; apply finite pushforward coherence and coherence of kernels.

source.place: Tag 05JU; coherence over locally Noetherian schemes.

proof.text: On an affine open U, the quasi-coherent cokernel has surjective quotient map on sections and kernel equal to the image of the normalization map. Its sections are zero iff that ring map is surjective, hence (using injectivity) iff the affine restriction of normalization is an isomorphism. Outside the conductor support, choose an affine neighbourhood with unit conductor, obtain this isomorphism and transport normality from the componentwise normalization stalk. Conversely at a normal point choose an affine open inside the normal open N; normalization is an isomorphism there, so its cokernel vanishes, the annihilator is the unit ideal, and the point is outside the support. Normalization stalks are normal domains by the coproduct open cover and the integral-closure stalk theorem over the function field. Thus the support is exactly the complement of N. Density of N gives nowhere density, and emptiness of support is equivalent both to unit conductor and to normality of all stalks.

source.place: Tags 035P, 0C3B and 0H7D; affine cokernel criterion and normal stalks.

proof.text: Specialize normalizedBlowup_calculus to the unit ideal (whose support is empty and whose affine ideals are finitely generated). Its smooth clause gives reduced T and the cartesian square of absolute componentwise normalizations. The canonical affine structure-sheaf base-change map is an isomorphism. Its compatibility with the structure-sheaf inclusion follows by transposing through the pullback-pushforward adjunction and evaluating on sections: the two expressions are the equal ring maps around the square. Pullback preserves cokernels, so this compatible pair of isomorphisms induces h^* C_S isomorphic to C_T.

source.place: Smooth normalization comparison, with canonical affine structure-sheaf base change and right exactness of pullback.

proof.text: Cover T by all affine V mapping into affine U in S. Coherence gives finite generation of C_S(U); pullback sections identify C_T(V) with B tensor_A C_S(U). Smoothness makes A to B flat. Apply finite flat annihilator base change, then the affine conductor formulas and ideal_comap_appLE. Extensionality for ideal sheaves on this affine cover gives the asserted equality. Identity and composition are the general comap_id and comap_comp identities. The pullback-sections calculation uses the already proved source-library exists_linearEquiv_pullback_sections for ordinary module pullback.

lean.statement: theorem conductor_smooth_base_change (S : Scheme.{u}) [AlgebraicGeometry.IsReduced S] (q : S ⟶ Spec (.of (ULift ℚ))) [LocallyOfFiniteType q] [QuasiCompact q] : IsFinite (Scheme.fromReducedNormalization S) ∧ (∀ U : S.Opens, Function.Injective ((Scheme.fromReducedNormalization S).app U).hom) ∧ RingedSpace.IsCoherent S.toRingedSpace (conductorCokernel S) ∧ RingedSpace.IsCoherent S.toRingedSpace (conductorIdeal S).toModules ∧ (∀ x : S, x ∈ ((conductorIdeal S).support : Set S) ↔ ¬ (IsDomain (S.presheaf.stalk x).carrier ∧ IsIntegrallyClosed (S.presheaf.stalk x).carrier)) ∧ IsNowhereDense ((conductorIdeal S).support : Set S) ∧ ((conductorIdeal S = ⊤) ↔ ∀ x : S, IsDomain (S.presheaf.stalk x).carrier ∧ IsIntegrallyClosed (S.presheaf.stalk x).carrier) ∧ (∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (h : T ⟶ S), QuasiCompact h → Smooth h → conductorIdeal T = (conductorIdeal S).comap h) ∧ ((conductorIdeal S).comap (𝟙 S) = conductorIdeal S) ∧ (∀ (T U : Scheme.{u}) (h : T ⟶ S) (g : U ⟶ T), (conductorIdeal S).comap (g ≫ h) = ((conductorIdeal S).comap h).comap g)
